planner.question: Does omitting the witness permit an efficient uniform counterexample generator for actual binary-clocked polynomial algorithms, and what remains of the same-U uniform formula-only route?
planner.strategy: Remove the witness from the generator output, charge exhaustive recovery in the self-describing program and vary the binary exponent rather than only the coefficient.
planner.alternative: Characterize uniform polynomial formula-only families by their total unary witness search relation.
planner.stop_rule: No cubic-stage infinitude, P!=NP claim, or reinterpretation of discovery cost as SAT decision cost.
literature_leads: Kleene recursion theorem and polynomial-overhead tape simulation (Sipser theorem 7.8); prior exact U diagonal discovery and quadratic-stage theorem. No novelty claim.

construct.claim: A total correct formula-only adversary for linear clocks necessarily takes Omega(m^3) time along a self-description family; on all binary polynomial clocks, if one exists, its runtime is at least 2^((3-o(1))m) along a family.
construct.scope: Same U and explicit selector input, original general descriptions and verifier; binary external clocks on individual programs only for discovery analysis.
construct.derivation: Run G on its own reconstructed description with coefficient or exponent 2^h, enumerate models of returned explicit p, and compare charged polynomial simulation times 2^(a n) to the actual clock. L>=n^3/2 and T>=L give the contradiction.
unresolved_steps: Unconditional unbounded cubic-stage failures or a polynomial cutoff.
candidate_tests: Explicit selector-only recovery, original writer and timeout checks, binary coefficient and exponent packing.

alternative.claim: For a fixed polynomial-time constructor of one satisfiable p_n per unary n, all-exponent residual infinitude along the family is equivalent to the absence of a polynomial-time unary witness finder.
alternative.scope: Given total constructor, same U stages; no existence claim for a hard constructor.
alternative.derivation: A finite exceptional set at one stage yields a polynomial unary solver; any unary polynomial solver embeds as one fixed description and succeeds by one uniform U stage.
unresolved_steps: Construct a genuinely hard formula-only family or prove a uniform cutoff.
candidate_tests: Small explicit formula-only selectors, exact exhaustive reconstruction and verification.

objections: Binary exponent is essential to the all-clock exponential bound.
A large runtime does not imply an equally large output formula.
All-clock generator existence is equivalent to P!=NP.

counterexample_candidates: A generator with a single fixed exponent need not face the binary-exponent adversary.
Separate fixed-k generators and existential lower bounds are not excluded.
